text: The customer and deceased-status read of rwb-source-data, the case state and timer read of rwb-case, the authorise operation of rwb-access and the rule-package and claim-approval read of rwb-decision are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and only rwb-case writes recovery_case, assignment and timer, while rwb-decision governs the rule rows and the approval; TSD S8 T5.2 names the interfaces only as module interfaces and publishes no operation name for these rows, so no name may be invented. The plan's C row for the slice is empty, so the rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.
read: FSD S8 A2.12.2 and A2.12.3.1; TSD S8 T5.2, T6.1 and T-A.1; context pack ownership rows and connection-matrix row S8; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 11 and 12.2; RWB-S8-E7003-CON sections 3, 7 AC3, 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision, before the contract is tagged
impact: The app story builds on Day 1 against four contract fakes with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a v_ace_* view or a recovery_case row fails the boundary test

text: The DEV rule rows are read as data at their version in force and evaluated inside the workflow activity, and the publication and the subscription run through the platform outbox and inbox library and the workflow kit; RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and RWB-PLT-E1071-CON are recorded as tracked absences and are not added to the metadata.
why: DP-04, DP-09 and DP-10 are not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, yet the branch evaluates the DEV route set of 22 rules, publishes EV-06 and runs DeviationWorkflow with five activities. Keeping the plan's H row unchanged and recording the kit dependencies as tracked is the only choice that does not invent a metadata value.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04, DP-09 and DP-10 and R5.4 class H; TSD S8 T4; context pack Temporal and Drools slides 5, 8 and 13 and ownership rows (events EV-06 and EV-07, no job, workflow DeviationWorkflow); split plan H list
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 3, 4, 12.3, 12.7 and 13; RWB-S8-E7003-CON sections 3, 12.3 and 13
confirm: Solution architect, the rule owner in rwb-decision and the platform workflow and event owners, before wave 4 starts
impact: The package arrives on its read with the version recorded with each outcome, and the kit dependencies are tracked rather than added to the metadata row

text: The contact stop of X3 is set on the deviation row and carried outward by rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 (EV-06), which rwb-comms consumes to suppress letters and calls and rwb-case consumes to pause the stage timer; this service sends no notice and calls no comms operation.
why: The connection matrix shows rwb-comms listening to S8 events and shows no REST edge from S8 to P6, and Event and Messaging Design v4 gives EV-06 the consumers timers and communications (contact stop). A REST call of this service to rwb-comms would contradict the matrix and would put a notice in the wrong owner's hands.
read: Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-06; context pack connection matrix (P6 row, column S8 = E) and ownership rows (events EV-06 and EV-07); FSD S8 A2.5 and A2.12.2
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 2, 4, 8 BR3, 12.3 and 12.9; RWB-S8-E7003-CON sections 7 AC4, 12.3 and 12.8
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-comms, when the event catalogue is baselined
impact: No comms client in the build, one consumer group on the event, and a notice that leaves against a stop is a comms defect and not a deviation defect

text: The customer, the deceased status and the policy link of the ACE view v_ace_customer are read only on the rwb-source-data data product with its freshness stamp; this service holds no v_ace_* grant and keeps no copy of the customer.
why: Architecture v5 slide 8 states that the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data, and DP-05 makes the owner's contract the only route to ACE data. The legacy Data table names v_ace_customer directly, which the target forbids.
read: Architecture v5 slide 8; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05 and R5.4; context pack naming and shared platform rules; TSD S8 T3.1 field list; legacy RWB-E7-003 Data table
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 2, 3, 8 BR1, 11 and 13; RWB-S8-E7003-CON sections 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-source-data, before the DB story of this service
impact: The customer facts arrive with the data date, a stale product holds the raise, and a v_ace_* grant added to the login fails the release gate

text: The death certificate and the claim evidence stay with rwb-document; this service receives their identifiers on DeviationRequest.documentIds, records the reference on the deviation and in the decision record, and reads no document row and stores no file.
why: No source publishes a document operation for S8 and the connection matrix shows no edge from S8 to P5, while the legacy Data table names document and API Specification v4 gives DeviationRequest a documentIds array. Taking the identifiers and leaving the evidence with its owner satisfies both.
read: API Specification v4, DeviationRequest (documentIds); context pack connection matrix (no S8-to-P5 edge) and ownership rows (tables: deviation only); FSD S8 A2.12.2 integration points (the Workbench document hub)
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 4, 8 BR10, 11 and 12.8; RWB-S8-E7003-CON sections 11 and 12.1
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-document, before the contract is tagged
impact: The pack, the storage reference and the retention stay with rwb-document, and the deviation holds only identifiers

text: The insurance claim reference and the heir notification reference are held in deviation.outcome of LOV-DEV-OUTCOME and in the decision record, and no new column, table or list is declared for them.
why: TSD S8 T3.1 gives deviation the ten fields DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the ownership rows give S8 one table, while no source names a claim-reference or notification-reference column. Adding one would be a value the builder invented.
read: TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.2; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8, DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045; context pack ownership rows (table deviation)
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 4, 11 and 13; RWB-S8-E7003-CON sections 11 and 12.7
confirm: Data steward of rwb-deviation and the owner of the DB story, before the schema is created
impact: The claim and the notification are evidenced by the decision record and the document identifiers, and the DB story may add a column later as a minor version

text: Legacy AC3 of RWB-E7-003, which pairs rule R-DEV-06 with X3 and the approval of an insurance claim, is copied verbatim, while the rule row in force names X6 and X7 as its codes; the row stands as published and its owner settles the code list.
why: The WP requires every owned legacy criterion to be copied word for word with its origin tag, and TSD S8 T4 and the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 both give R-DEV-06 the condition deviation_code in (X6,X7). Rewording the criterion or the rule would invent a business value, so the conflict is carried and assigned.
read: Legacy RWB-E7-003 AC3; TSD S8 T4 rule table; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4, R-DEV-06; FSD S8 A2.12.3.1
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP sections 7, 8 and 16; RWB-S8-E7003-CON section 7 AC2
confirm: Rule owner in rwb-decision and the business owner of S8, before wave 4 starts
impact: The branch builds both paths: R-DEV-03 for X3 as published, and the R-DEV-06 approval gate for the codes the row names, so neither reading is lost

text: No approval or status gate blocks this work: the BRDs and PRDs are not approved in this run, so both stories carry status Draft (realignment v1), the contract baseline is tagged by its own review, and the PRD reference stays Pending (C1).
why: D-RCV-60 removes the human approval stop and the WP states the status Draft (realignment v1); Template and Rules R8.5 places the PRDs after this stage, so no PRD can be cited yet and its reference is a placeholder by design.
read: Template and Rules v1 R8.1, R8.5 and R9; root AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10; work package B2-S8-003
applied_in: RWB-S8-E7003-APP metadata and section 3; RWB-S8-E7003-CON metadata and section 3
confirm: Coordinator of the realignment run, at the stage close
impact: The build may start on Day 1 against the Draft baseline and the fakes, and the PRD reference is replaced when the PRD exists
